Optical flow introduces temporal coherence but requires dense sampling. K-Means assumes static color priors while teams may swap uniforms. Perspective transformation linearizes geometry but breaks under extreme parallax. Dualities emerge: detection vs. tracking (set membership vs. trajectory continuity), color vs. motion (static vs. dynamic cues). Failure modes include: 1) Occlusion-induced label switching between YOLO detections, 2) Flow divergence from sudden accelerations, 3) Color confusion in mixed lighting. Anti-collinearity is enforced by decoupling posterior updates: team labels are updated via K-Means only when sufficient color variance exists, otherwise fallback to nearest-neighbor tracking.
